title: JavaScript objects, properties, descriptors, and reflection
concepts: Objects as property collections with identity
Property keys and own versus inherited lookup

inventory.title: Object creation, keys, and property definitions
Prototype operations, integrity, and Object methods

accuracyFacts: All property keys are strings or Symbols. Other computed keys are converted with ToPropertyKey; own and inherited are separate from enumerable and non-enumerable.

Object literal spread and Object.assign copy enumerable own string and Symbol properties by reading source values; accessors run and the destination receives data values. Object.assign writes through target [[Set]] and can invoke target setters, while object spread creates data properties on the new object.

Object.keys, values, and entries include only own enumerable string keys. getOwnPropertyNames includes all own string keys; getOwnPropertySymbols includes all own Symbol keys; getOwnPropertyDescriptors includes all own keys and descriptor records. Ordinary own-key ordering places array-index keys first in ascending numeric order, then other strings in creation order, then Symbols in creation order.

Property descriptors are either data descriptors or accessor descriptors; they cannot combine value/writable with get/set. For a new property, omitted descriptor fields default to false or undefined. When redefining an existing property, omitted fields preserve current values. defineProperty throws when the requested change violates non-configurable property rules.

Object.hasOwn checks direct ownership, including non-enumerable and Symbol keys; it works with null-prototype objects and shadowed hasOwnProperty names. The in operator checks own or inherited presence. hasOwnProperty can be shadowed or absent.

Object.groupBy groups an iterable into arrays and returns an object whose prototype is null. Its callback result is converted to a property key; use Map.groupBy when group keys must remain arbitrary values instead of property keys.

Object.fromEntries consumes an iterable of key-value pairs and creates own data properties, including Symbol keys. Its property creation safely treats the string __proto__ as a data key rather than invoking the legacy prototype setter.
Object.create(null) creates an object with no prototype and no inherited Object methods; use Object.hasOwn or other static reflection rather than assuming obj.hasOwnProperty exists.

Object.assign is shallow, copies values rather than full descriptors, may partially modify the target before a thrown assignment, and ignores null/undefined sources. Object.freeze/seal/preventExtensions affect only the object's own structural/property attributes and are shallow; referenced nested objects remain mutable.

Object.preventExtensions prevents new own properties; seal additionally makes existing own properties non-configurable; freeze additionally makes own data properties non-writable. A non-empty typed array cannot be frozen in current ECMAScript implementations because its indexed elements cannot satisfy frozen integrity constraints.

Changing an object's prototype dynamically with Object.setPrototypeOf can be costly and difficult to reason about; prefer Object.create at creation when a custom prototype is needed. Object.prototype.__proto__ and __defineGetter__/__defineSetter__/__lookupGetter__/__lookupSetter__ are legacy/deprecated compatibility APIs.
Object.is uses SameValue semantics: NaN equals itself and positive zero differs from negative zero. It is not the same relation as ==, ===, or SameValueZero.
